note: The TICK-LIST INPUT (Library/Nova/tick-list.json — learn-and-drive v3 P2, §3.3 step 1): the cheat candidates the website proposes for the kit's Nova Capture window, and whether each whole file is REFUSED. Run by BOTH sides: the kit's TickList.Refusal (the check SyncNova runs before writing, and the reader of the file on disk) and the website's tickListRefusal (apps/renderer/src/game-ads/learn/tick-list.ts, which buildTickList runs before anything is sent). 'doc' is the document (serialised as JSON by each runner); 'text' is a file given VERBATIM instead; 'generate' {count: N} is a document of N candidates 'raw cheat0' … 'raw cheat<N-1>'; 'commandLength' L is a document of ONE candidate 'raw ' followed by L-4 'x'. 'maxCandidates' and 'maxCommandLength' are the caps both sides refuse above (the kit's Levers.MaxLevers and Levers.MaxLeverLength; the site's MAX_LEVERS and MAX_LEVER_LENGTH). For a case that is NOT refused, 'risky' lists — sorted — the commands BOTH sides call risky (the kit's CheatRisk.Why, the site's tickListRisk): by a word root of the press guard or the cheat roots (give, grant, gift, server), or by what the file says of that exact command (kind give / reset / purchase, or any risk label). A delivered file can only RAISE a command's risk, never lower it. The file is DATA: a case one side disagrees with is a finding to take to both sides, never a line to edit here. Not covered, on purpose: a $schemaVersion written 1.0 (the kit reads a float, the site's JSON.parse reads 1) and a JSON comment (the kit's reader skips it, JSON.parse refuses it) — the site never writes either. 'keysKnownTo0_10' is the per-candidate key set a 0.10.x kit's reader knows (v0.10.0 Editor/Adapter/TickList.cs:130; any other key and it refuses the whole send): the server hands a kit before 0.11.0 each list WITHOUT 'check' (apps/api/src/studio/studio-capture-job.ts tickListForKit). The API spec strips every case that is read and holds what is left to this set; the kit's runner checks that the stripped list is still read. Kit 0.13.4 adds expect 'becomes' with a numeric 'value' (finite, |value| <= 1e15) on a get check or a watched snapshot: a set-to cheat is proven by the value it BECOMES; the server hands a 0.13.2/0.13.3 kit each list without those checks (tickListForKit). Fix 4 (2026-09-28, invariant 182): a candidate whose command is the set-value template `set Type.Member {v}` may carry a `becomes` check whose value is that command's own placeholder (the string "{v}") and never one fixed number; no other candidate's check names a placeholder. The server hands a kit before 0.14.0 each list WITHOUT set-value template candidates (an older kit refuses a template, and with it the whole list). Invariant 190 (kit 0.14.2): a top-level 'needed' list — the levers the studio's current work needs, each {command, label?} — rides beside 'candidates'; its command follows a candidate's command rule and is never a template (the set-value shape included: a shot and a story run the filled command); a label is 1–80 plain characters; a command is listed once; at most maxCandidates entries. For a case that is read, 'needed' lists the needed commands in file order and 'neededRisky' — sorted — those BOTH sides call risky (the same CheatRisk.Why / tickListRisk, over the file's candidates). The server hands a kit before 0.14.2 each list WITHOUT 'needed' (tickListForKit).
